subject: Banking
title: Embedded Finance Everywhere
description: A micro-lesson that makes Embedded Finance Everywhere usable.

hook.text: Buy a car and get financing from the dealership app. Embedded finance puts banking inside every other product.

buildup.text: Shopify offers loans to merchants. Uber provides debit cards to drivers.

discovery.text: Infrastructure providers like Unit, Treasury Prime, and Bond let any company offer bank accounts and cards via API.

twist.text: Embedded finance could make standalone banks obsolete.

climax.text: Finance is becoming a feature, not a destination. The bank disappears into the platform where you spend your time.

punchline.text: Banking inside every app. Finance becomes a feature, not a separate product.

quiz.question: What is embedded finance?
options: Financial services built into non-financial platforms and apps

details.summary: Embedded finance integrates banking services directly into non-financial apps and platforms. You can get a loan while shopping, insurance while booking travel, or a bank account through your employer, all without visiting a bank.
details.whyItMatters: Embedded finance makes banking invisible and contextual, meeting people at the exact moment of financial need. It could fundamentally shift power from banks to the platforms where people already spend their time.
takeaways: Shopify Capital lends to merchants directly within its platform
Embedded finance is projected to generate over $230 billion in revenue by 2025
Banks provide the backend while brands own the customer relationship

faq.question: What is embedded finance in everyday life?
faq.answer: Buy-now-pay-later at checkout, instant insurance when booking a flight, getting paid early through your employer's HR app, or opening a savings account within a ride-sharing app are all examples of banking embedded into non-bank experiences.

faq.question: Are banks worried about embedded finance?
faq.answer: Banks provide the regulated backend infrastructure for most embedded finance. They earn fees as service providers but lose the direct customer relationship and the data that comes with it, which may erode their long-term competitive position.
